A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Tiled Prompts research, with matching authors, core framework, and experiments. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original image/video super-resolution experiments comparing prompt variants, including quantitative quality and alignment scores, runtime measurements, and qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 reports original experiments, including retained prompt comparisons, reference-based evaluations, additional backbone evaluations, and a CFG-scale ablation.

M1.justification: The core tiled conditioning, aggregation algorithm, and context-assisted video prompting remain. However, the reported image prompt-extraction instruction changes from the detailed two-image comparison in v1 Appendix A.2 to the short image-keyword instruction in v2 Appendix B.2, a limited procedural revision.

E1.justification: v2 adds image evaluations on SEPE8K, DIV2K, and DIV8K, substantially broadening the evaluated data beyond the retained image benchmarks. Video dataset coverage remains VideoLQ, RealVSR, and MVSR4x. LSDIR2048 is a newly selected subset of the already-used LSDIR dataset.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 add a no-text Null comparator alongside the retained Global and Global+Local comparisons. Appendix C applies these prompt comparisons within additional host models—OSEDiff, DiffVSR, and Upscale-A-Video—while retaining the same prompt-comparator structure.

E3.justification: v2 adds reference evaluation using 2048×2048 ground truth and PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, DISTS, and FID, including a 153-image LSDIR subset. Additional protocols evaluate OSEDiff on 800 DIV2K and 1500 DIV8K training-split images and sweep eight STAR CFG scales from 2.5 to 20. These substantially extend the evaluation design.

E4.justification: v2 Figure 6 adds a systematic CFG-sensitivity analysis absent from v1. Appendix C tests whether prompting gains transfer across additional SR backbones, and the qualitative case coverage expands. Some v1 misguidance examples are reused in v2 Figure 8 rather than constituting wholly new evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The additional tables and CFG curves retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Numerous existing scores change: Table 1's LSDIR1K Local CLIPScore changes from 27.5817 to 27.2274, and Table 2's MVSR Local MUSIQ changes from 36.0415 to 68.4642. v2 also adds Null, reference-based, additional-backbone, and CFG results. These are revised or newly reported results; unexplained setting differences prevent interpreting the revisions as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 adds a unified Gaussian diffusion/flow formulation, Lemma 1, two propositions, and Appendix A proofs connecting guidance errors, conditional mutual information, posterior KL divergence, and path-space discrepancies. Ideal-prompt sufficiency and local-prompt informativeness assumptions substantially extend v1's simpler sparsity and CFG-error analysis.

C1.justification: v2 adds a central claimed contribution that misguidance can be formally minimized by lowering an information-theoretic bound. Its abstract also emphasizes fidelity gains where v1 emphasized text alignment. The unified image/video prompting contribution remains; renaming sparsity and misguidance as omission and commission largely preserves those earlier concepts.

C2.justification: v2 introduces a substantial information-theoretic mechanism explanation, interprets measured CFG sensitivity as amplification of prompt errors, and explicitly argues that semantic relevance rather than additional tokens explains Local versus Global+Local performance. These extend v1's semantic-interference discussion. Both versions retain the limitation that VLMs can misinterpret or hallucinate content.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page link, checkpoint access information for additional backbones, the global-video extraction instruction, RTX 3090 timing hardware, and CFG sweep settings. It revises the image instruction while retaining the local-video instruction. v1's explicit video bicubic-upsampling and central-valid-region aggregation details are omitted, without establishing that those procedures changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds supporting references for diffusion/flow theory, new datasets, reference metrics, and DiffVSR. The existing text-guided SR survey and novelty positioning around localized VLM prompting remain largely intact; this extends supporting literature more than it revises the relationship to competing approaches.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: preliminaries and method sections are rewritten around misguidance and its theoretical analysis, separate image/video results become joint quality and prompt-evaluation discussions, and appendices are restructured. Terminology changes throughout, and the earlier general training-strategy section and generic impact statement disappear.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout, resizing and relocating retained figures and tables. v2 adds reference and backbone tables, Null rows, and the CFG plot, while expanding and reorganizing qualitative galleries. Main Figures 1–5 and several appendix examples are retained rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: Reference-based evaluation, additional-backbone tests, and the CFG ablation strengthen empirical support beyond v1's no-reference quality evaluation on two backbones. The gain is tempered by unexplained revisions to existing scores and an overstrong new theoretical claim: lowering the bound in Propositions 1–2 does not itself establish reduced actual misguidance. The added validation supports a limited net improvement.
